correctness.rationale: Enumerated every one of 6^n labeled complete strict three-candidate profiles for n=1..5 independently by positional Borda and pairwise-majority Copeland scoring. No different singleton outcomes occur through n=4; at n=5 precisely 60 of 7776 profiles conflict. Reconstructed the 3 BCA +2 CAB witness with Borda vector (2,6,7), pairwise margins (A-B,A-C,B-C)=(-1,-5,1), and unique Copeland winner B versus Borda C. The six anonymous conflicts each have multinomial weight 10 and constitute one six-profile candidate orbit, yielding anonymous incidence 1/42 and labeled incidence 5/648. The finite exhaustive proof only claims n<=5 under no external tiebreak.

originality.rationale: A classic five-voter Borda/Condorcet counterexample is prior and explicitly not claimed as novel. The assessed claim is the complete first different-unique-winner layer: strict lower-bound exclusion, exact 60/7776 incidence, six anonymous profiles, and exactly one orbit. Author-shared full text of Favardin-Lepelley-Serais treats manipulation under fixed tie-breaking, not this count. A highly relevant inaccessible older coincidence-probability source remains a material originality risk rather than an automatic failure.
residual_risks: The highly relevant 1978 Gehrlein-Fishburn paper was inaccessible in full despite bibliographic searches and an authorized institutional attempt; it could contain an exact finite-n coincidence formula.
1976 Fishburn-Gehrlein classic results and election-census appendices could imply the 60 count without printing it.
A standard five-voter Condorcet/Borda reversal witness is known; originality is ONLY the complete first-layer count and single orbit.

value.rationale: First disagreement between two canonical aggregation principles, conditional on genuinely unique outcomes, is mathematically natural and eliminates artifacts of tie breaking. Exact finite electorate incidence and complete one-orbit explanation are useful small-instance structural benchmarks even though existence of a five-voter counterexample is standard. Coverage is restricted to three candidates and at most five voters.

final_claim: With three candidates under strict complete ballots, Borda and Copeland have different singleton winners first at five voters; 60 of 7776 labeled and 6 of 252 anonymous profiles conflict, all forming one candidate-relabeling orbit.
limitations: Strict unique-winner only, three candidates and n<=5; the existence of a 5-voter Borda-Condorcet paradox is known.
Gehrlein-Fishburn (1978) full text unavailable despite search and authorized attempt; exact finite coincidence formula remains material originality risk.
